title: The frontend rejects an internal reference containing a space, hyphen or slash; DR1 accepts whatever the user's own system calls the consignment.

finding.frontend: The field invites 'any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment', but only letters, numbers and underscores get through. Typing ACME-2026/01, or a reference with a space in it, returns the page with 'Internal reference must only contain letters, numbers and underscores'. There is also a 58-character ceiling, with 'Internal reference must be 58 characters or less' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:75-82).
finding.prototype: DR1 asks the same optional question with the same label and the same hint, and imposes no rule on it at all: the submitted value is trimmed and stored, and no length or character check runs (app/routes.js:9240-9244). A user pastes in whatever reference their own records use.
finding.difference: Drop the character rule so hyphens, slashes, spaces and full stops are accepted — the whole point of the field is that it is the user's own reference and the service does not read it. Keep a length ceiling if downstream storage needs one, but say the limit in the hint rather than only in an error, and confirm 58 is a real constraint rather than an arbitrary one, because DR1 states no limit.
finding.falsifiedBy: Submitting DR1's origin page with an internal reference containing a hyphen and being returned to the page with an error about the characters used.
finding.correction: Verified sound. WHERE EACH SIDE ENFORCES: the frontend enforces at the page and only at the page — pattern('internalReferenceNumber', /^\w*$/) and maxText at 58 in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:63-82. \w is letters, digits and underscore, so a space, hyphen, slash or full stop is rejected exactly as claimed. There is no obligation on the field at all (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/origin.js carries only countryOfOrigin, regionOfOriginCodeRequirement and regionOfOriginCode), so nothing else in the service touches it. DR1 enforces nowhere: the POST trims the value and stores it, validateOriginOfImport does not look at it, and hasOriginDetails does not test it — so no length or character rule exists on that side (app/routes.js:9240-9244, 231-245, 246-263). This is the only one of the six validation claims where one side has a rule the other has nowhere at all. Both sides label the field the same and both treat it as optional. HOW CHECKED: read both validators, the origin obligation section and DR1's origin POST and completeness helpers.
